prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an open outdoor paved courtyard covered in rows of egg cartons on the left and a multi-tiered wheeled rack of blue boards on the right, with a blue board held within arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m) below the camera wearer's viewpoint across all five frames. In Frame 1, two workers stand ahead to the left of the rack—one in red upright at ~4–5 m facing the camera wearer and another in black bent over ~1.5 m to his left at ~5–6 m—before the wearer turns left and tilts downward across Frames 2–4 toward the ground (~1–2 m away) and then turns right in Frame 5 to face the rack (~1–2 m on the right) and the two workers (~4–5 m ahead, ~1 m apart, both facing toward the wearer with the worker in black holding a board within his reach). In Frame 4, the bright foreground clearly separates the elevated blue board and cartons (~0.4–0.5 m) and the wearer's supporting right arm and partially occluded left hand from the darker ground and left foot (~1.2 m) directly below. Compared to RGB alone, the continuous luminance gradient makes the ground plane's recession and the vertical step between the held board and the floor immediately apparent even where repetitive carton textures flatten perspective. However, the map is unreliable on the thin metal frame of the rack, which merges into the background depth, and in Frame 4 where the ground appears abnormally dark relative to Frames 2 and 3 despite a similar viewing distance.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and background entities across the courtyard, detecting three people in Frame 1—the bent worker in black (~5–6 m, center-left), the standing worker in red (~4–5 m, center, ~1.5 m right of the first), and a tiny distant figure (~15–20 m behind the first worker's shoulder)—while leaving the ground, egg cartons, and wheeled rack unsegmented. As the camera wearer turns left and looks down in Frame 2, only the lower legs of a person at the upper-right edge (~3–4 m away) remain in view, and Frame 3 is completely empty of masks as the viewpoint faces the ground grid of cartons (~1–3 m). In Frame 4, at close range (~0.3–1.2 m), the map segments the wearer's extended right arm on the lower right and left foot on the lower center as distinct person instances within arm's reach, and in Frame 5 it re-detects the two upright workers side by side ~4–5 m ahead (~1 m apart, with the worker in black slightly nearer and partly occluding the rack beside the worker in red). This map makes it easier than RGB alone to spot the tiny distant person in Frame 1 and to separate the overlapping silhouettes of the two workers in Frame 5. However, it is highly unreliable for object classes and completeness, misclassifying two moulded egg cartons on the held board in Frame 4 as 'pizza' and a blue shelf on the rack in Frame 5 as 'boat', while failing to segment the wearer's partially occluded left hand in Frame 4 and all other boards and cartons.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, capturing only the upright worker in red in Frame 1 (~4–5 m ahead, left of the rack), the wearer's own right hand in Frame 4 (~0.4 m ahead, lower right), and the worker in black in Frame 5 (~4 m ahead, center-right). In Frame 1, the yellow body skeleton shows the worker in red standing in three-quarter profile facing forward and slightly left with his head oriented toward the camera wearer and his arms hanging within reach of the adjacent rack, while the bent worker ~1.5 m to his left is completely missed. Frames 2 and 3 contain no skeletal detections at all because the nearby person at the top-right of Frame 2 is mostly out of view above the knees and Frame 3 shows only the ground and the bottom edge of the held board. In Frame 4, a magenta hand skeleton highlights the curled fingers and thumb of the wearer's right hand gripping the bottom edge of the blue board within arm's reach, and in Frame 5 a yellow body skeleton shows the worker in black facing toward the camera wearer with both elbows bent and forearms raised to hold a board at chest height. While the skeletons clarify the exact finger articulation under the board edge in Frame 4 and limb joint positions in Frames 1 and 5 better than RGB alone, the map is unreliable because it misses the bent worker in Frame 1, the wearer's partially occluded left hand and foot in Frame 4, the second standing worker in Frame 5, and all hand skeletons on the distant workers.
